title.narrative: Reclaiming Traditional Communal Irrigation Pools “BIRKET” of South Lebanon

description.narrative:
Lebanon’s prolonged drought, degraded communal ponds (birkets), and weak routine O&M threaten irrigation, livelihoods, and hydraulic heritage in South Lebanon. The project delivers two outcomes: (1) a solid, public evidence base on South Lebanon’s communal reservoirs is created and used to inspire preservation and policy action; (2) water heritage is preserved; a flagship birket on the trail is restored and preserved; and residents resume reliable use of its irrigation water. Outputs: 1.1 a multidisciplinary dossier on all mapped birkets is compiled and published; 1.2 research is translated into accessible media products (15 reels, a broadcast-quality documentary, and a travelling exhibition). 2.1 Water Inventory toolkit is adopted and trail/museum designs are endorsed by stakeholders; 2.2 the flagship birket is rehabilitated into a functioning reservoir and an attractive public space. Key activities: deep-archive and field ethnography; report/infographics/maps/photos; co-design studios with landscape students and communities; Water Museum concept with WAMU-Net; heritage-compatible works; adoption of simple O&M bylaws and irrigation schedules.
The outcome(s), outputs and key activities as well as performance indicators and associated information are described in more detail in Annex A. Results Framework and Annex D. Monitoring and Evaluation (M&E) Framework.
